questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code authenticates callers and verifies credentials? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
jwt.get_unverified_header reads the token header before the signature has been checked. Why is that not a way for an attacker to choose how the token is verified?
choices: The header is encrypted so the attacker cannot change it
The header is compared with the claims after decoding, which catches tampering
PyJWT ignores the header for any token that has an exp claim
The kid is only used to look up a key in a local table and the accepted algorithms are fixed by the server, so the attacker cannot select an algorithm or a key outside the table

questions.prompt: A caller presents a valid access token that has the scope notifications:read but not notifications:send, and posts to /v1/notifications. What response do they get and why?
choices: 403 Insufficient scope, because authentication succeeded and require_scope rejected the principal
401, because the token is not valid for this endpoint
422, because the scope check happens during body validation

questions.prompt: A request presents an API key with an unknown key id and another presents a known key id with a wrong secret. What does ApiKeyAuthenticator do?
choices: Raises different errors so support can tell them apart in the response
Returns immediately for the unknown id without hashing, because there is no record to compare against
Hashes the presented secret and compares it in constant time in both cases, then raises the same AuthError message
Falls back to checking the key against the bearer token verifier
